name: Circadian Architecture and Temporal Light Regulation
mechanism_chain_provenance: NEWLY ESTABLISHED in LIGHT-I — gap stub only; closely related to CIRCADIAN_ARCH_REG_001 (L2) but addresses the design-decision level rather than the biological mechanism level
note: This template encodes the architectural design decision layer — the specific building parameters whose values determine whether the circadian channel delivers adequate stimulus — as distinct from the biological mechanism template (CIRCADIAN_ARCH_REG_001) which encodes the neural pathway. These are complementary templates operating at different levels of the causal chain.

mechanism_chain.description: Architectural design parameters: WFR, glazing VT and spectral transmission, orientation, room depth, ceiling height, shading system type

data.finding: Window-to-floor ratio, glazing visible transmittance, orientation, and room depth are the primary determinants of daylight availability at the workplane
data.effect: Architectural parameters predict >85% of variance in annual daylight metrics

justification.backing: This is a constitutive relationship: the listed parameters mathematically determine the daylight delivery envelope. No empirical study required — physics and geometry constrain the outcome.
justification.qualifier: Occupant behavior (shading deployment, furniture placement) modifies actual delivery within the architectural envelope.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if occupant behavior dominates architectural constraints (e.g., all blinds permanently closed).

mechanism_chain.description: → Spatial daylight autonomy (sDA) and Useful Daylight Illuminance (UDI) distributions in occupied zones (Reinhart metrics)

data.finding: Climate-based daylight modeling (CBDM) predicts annual sDA300/50% and UDI distributions from architectural parameters and TMY weather data
data.paradigm: Daylight simulation validation against field measurement
data.effect: CBDM predictions correlate r > 0.85 with field-measured illuminance

justification.backing: The Reinhart CBDM method is the industry standard for predicting annual daylight performance. sDA and UDI are established metrics adopted by LEED, WELL, and IES standards.
justification.qualifier: Simulation accuracy depends on accurate material reflectances, sky model, and shading schedule assumptions.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if actual shading behavior differs substantially from simulation assumptions; or if TMY weather data does not represent actual conditions.

mechanism_chain.description: → Post-processed via Spitschan CCT-to-melanopic conversion → estimated floor-plate melanopic irradiance distribution

data.finding: CIE S 026:2018 provides standard melanopic action spectrum and conversion factors from photopic illuminance to melanopic EDI for standard illuminants
data.effect: Enables melanopic irradiance estimation from photopic illuminance and CCT

justification.backing: The Spitschan conversion methodology allows post-processing of photopic daylight simulations to estimate melanopic delivery. This is essential because standard CBDM tools output photopic lux, not melanopic EDI.
justification.qualifier: Conversion accuracy depends on accurate CCT estimation; daylight CCT varies with sky condition, time of day, and glazing spectral transmission.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if glazing has non-standard spectral characteristics that distort the CCT-to-melanopic relationship; or if interior surface reflectances substantially modify spectral composition.

mechanism_chain.description: → Compared against CHRONO_LIGHT_ENTRAINMENT_001 daily integral minimum (150 m-lux·h) and CIRCADIAN_ARCH_REG_001 maintenance threshold (87 m-lux for 2h)

data.finding: Minimum 150 m-lux·hours daily daytime melanopic dose for stable entrainment maintenance; minimum 87 m-lux for 2 continuous hours for acute maintenance
data.source: Kronauer model derivation; Figueiro et al. (2017); cross-reference to CHRONO_LIGHT_ENTRAINMENT_001 and CIRCADIAN_ARCH_REG_001
data.effect: Threshold values derived from circadian physiology templates

justification.backing: The threshold comparison links architectural daylight delivery to the biologically-derived thresholds in companion templates. This is the critical bridge from design parameters to physiological outcomes.
justification.qualifier: Threshold values have uncertainty ranges (100-250 m-lux·h for integral; 50-125 m-lux for acute). The comparison is probabilistic, not deterministic.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if individual chronotype variation requires personalized thresholds that cannot be addressed at the architectural design level.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.description: → If thresholds met: circadian maintenance channel active

data.finding: Buildings meeting sDA300/50% in climate zones with adequate daylight availability deliver sufficient melanopic stimulus for circadian maintenance in majority of occupants
data.source: Figueiro et al. (2017); WELL Building Standard v2 circadian lighting requirements
data.effect: sDA300 serves as acceptable proxy for circadian adequacy

justification.backing: The WELL standard's adoption of sDA300/50% as a circadian proxy reflects expert consensus that photopic daylight adequacy generally implies melanopic adequacy. This step activates the downstream biological templates.
justification.qualifier: sDA300 is an imperfect proxy — it does not guarantee morning timing, which is critical for circadian phase. Orientation and occupancy schedule must also align.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if occupants work night shifts; or if building orientation concentrates daylight delivery in afternoon rather than morning.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.description: → If thresholds not met: gap quantified; supplementary electric lighting specification required

data.finding: Circadian-effective electric lighting can supplement inadequate daylight; 300 lux at 4000K delivers approximately 186 m-lux mEDI
data.source: Lucas et al. (2014); CIE S 026 conversion tables
data.effect: Electric lighting parameters specified to fill melanopic gap

justification.backing: When daylight is insufficient, electric lighting with appropriate spectrum and intensity can provide the melanopic stimulus. This step quantifies the gap and specifies the supplementary requirement.
justification.qualifier: Electric lighting supplements are less effective than daylight due to: (a) typically lower irradiance; (b) potentially inappropriate timing (evening use delays phase); (c) reduced dynamic range compared to daylight.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if electric lighting is not properly controlled for circadian timing; bright evening electric light could worsen circadian outcomes despite meeting melanopic intensity targets.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

temporal_rhythm.note: Spatial daylight autonomy of 300 lux (sDA300/50%) — the LEED/WELL standard metric — is a reasonable but imperfect proxy for circadian adequacy. At 300 photopic lux from daylight (approximately 4500–5500K effective CCT under clear sky), melanopic irradiance is approximately 210–270 m-lux mEDI — well above the 87 m-lux threshold. However, sDA300 is met at 50% of occupied hours, which does not guarantee morning delivery timing. Threshold of 0.55 reflects conservative architectural target that correlates with acceptable circadian delivery in most climate zones.
temporal_rhythm.source: Reinhart et al. (2006); Spasojević et al. (2021); WELL standard v2

minimum_morning_illuminance_CCT4000K.note: 300 lux at 4000K delivers approximately 186 m-lux mEDI — above the 87 m-lux maintenance threshold. This is the minimum supplementary lighting specification for circadian adequacy in zones that cannot achieve sDA300 from daylight alone.

minimum_morning_illuminance_CCT2700K.note: If warm-white (2700K) lighting is specified for aesthetic reasons, 500 lux is required to match the melanopic delivery of 300 lux at 4000K.

spatial_configuration.note: At a room depth equal to 2× the head-of-window height from the floor, the daylit melanopic irradiance falls to approximately 62% of the window-wall value. At 3× ceiling height depth: approximately 35%. Beyond this depth, supplementary lighting is required for circadian adequacy.
spatial_configuration.source: Reinhart CBDM modeling; Boyce (2003) daylight penetration data

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Indirect — via CIRCADIAN_ARCH_REG_001; this template establishes the architectural conditions whose adequacy or inadequacy determines the IC2 interaction strength in the circadian cluster
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Direct: shading system design determines whether occupants have AX4 control over their light exposure. Manual Venetian blinds provide high AX4; automated electrochromic glazing without occupant override provides low AX4 despite high apparent sophistication.

higher_order_principle: Architectural design parameters → supplementary lighting specification pathway: The mechanism by which circadian architecture and temporal light regulation operates
